# Spec: Web App Business Hours Uptime

Status: draft
Topic: web-app-uptime

## Purpose

This spec defines the operational requirements for a web application that must remain available to users during designated business hours in a single timezone. It covers deployment practices, support procedures, monitoring, alerting, and service level objectives to ensure reliable operation during working hours.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criterion (Given / When / Then) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Health checks must run continuously | Given the app is deployed, when a health check endpoint is called, then it responds with status 200 within 5 seconds | open |
| R2 | Alerts fire within 5 minutes of service degradation | Given monitoring detects error rate >5% or latency >2s p99, when this condition persists for 1 minute, then an alert is sent to on-call support | open |
| R3 | On-call support is assigned during business hours | Given business hours in the defined timezone are active, when a critical alert fires, then an on-call engineer is notified within 5 minutes | open |
| R4 | Deployments can be executed in <10 minutes | Given code is merged to main and tests pass, when deployment is triggered, then the app is live in production within 10 minutes | open |
| R5 | Rollback capability must be maintained | Given a deployment causes user-facing errors, when rollback is initiated, then the previous stable version is restored within 5 minutes | open |
| R6 | Incident escalation path is defined | Given a critical issue is unresolved after 30 minutes, when escalation criteria are met, then the on-call manager is paged | open |
| R7 | Service level: 99% uptime during business hours | Given any calendar day, when business hours pass in the defined timezone, then the app must be available (responding to requests) for at least 99% of that window | open |
| R8 | Maintenance windows are scheduled outside business hours | Given maintenance is required, when it is scheduled, then it occurs outside the business hours window in the defined timezone | open |
| R9 | Runbooks exist for common incidents | Given a on-call engineer receives an alert, when they access runbook documentation, then they find step-by-step remediation for the top 5 incident types | open |
| R10 | Database backups occur daily | Given the app stores persistent data, when the backup job runs, then a restorable backup is created and verified daily outside business hours | open |

## Non-goals

- This spec does not cover after-hours support or 24/7 operation
- Performance optimization beyond the latency thresholds stated is out of scope
- Capacity planning for future growth is not addressed here
- Multi-region or disaster recovery is not addressed
- User SLA agreements beyond the uptime percentage stated

## Open questions

- UNKNOWN: Which timezone defines "business hours"? Owner: Product or Operations lead.
- UNKNOWN: What are the exact business hours (e.g., 9 AM–5 PM, Monday–Friday)? Owner: Product or Operations lead.
- UNKNOWN: What constitutes a "critical" incident requiring escalation? Owner: Incident commander or On-call manager.
- ASSUMED — Error rate threshold is 5% and p99 latency is 2 seconds for alert triggers; these should be validated against production baselines and user impact.
- ASSUMED — Rollback to a previous version is always safe; a testing strategy to verify this should be defined elsewhere.
- ASSUMED — On-call rotation exists and contact information is maintained; ownership and escalation contacts are defined in a separate runbook.

## References

None at this time.
